meta.title: The Rich Cat
meta.textType: story: the main idea of a picture story

paragraphs: On Thursday, Lily opened an email from her pen pal, Grace, in Singapore. Grace liked to draw, and Lily liked to read. Grace sent six pictures and a short note. Lily was very happy. The note said, "This is my picture story. What is it about?" Lily showed the pictures to Mia in the school library before the club hour.

In picture one, a rich cat lived at the top of a tall skyscraper. Everything in his big room was gold. The room was big, and it was very quiet. In picture two, he collected shiny cups, rings, and coins. In picture three, he sat alone at the window every night. He looked at the lights of the city, and he did not smile. He had no friend to talk to.

In picture four, a small bird suddenly landed on the window. The cat gave the bird a gold ring, but the bird did not want it. The bird sang a small song. In picture five, the cat took a chess game out of a box. The cat and the bird played chess on the floor. The cat laughed for the first time. In picture six, they sat together at the window and smiled. The gold things stayed in the box.

"I know the main idea," said Mia. Mia looked at the pictures again. "The cat has many things, but he wants a friend." "I think so too," said Lily. "The pictures show it. Nobody needs words." Lily counted six pictures on the screen. "Which picture do you like best?" asked Mia. "I like picture six," said Lily.

That evening, Lily wrote an answer to Grace. "Your picture story is excellent," she wrote. "The cat is rich, but his friend is the best thing in his life." Lily put the story on Explorers' Blog, and Teacher Kim read it first.
text.summary: Lily gets an email from her pen pal Grace with a picture story of six pictures. A rich cat lives alone at the top of a skyscraper until a small bird comes to his window.
